correctness.rationale: Writing λ_j=(c_j−u_j·x)/h_j, the facet coordinates of the foot of v_i are q_ij=−(h_i/h_j)g_ij. The affine projection of x onto F_i has coordinates λ_j+λ_i q_ij. Inside T, nonnegativity is precisely λ_j≥(−q_ij)_+λ_i, and subtracting these multiples from λ_j and scaling λ_i by 1+b_i sends this region bijectively to the standard simplex. Its apex has altitude h_i/(1+b_i), proving the volume ratio. Strictly interior foot and closed-foot conventions differ on null hyperplanes; the latter is the closure of the former. Linearity yields the mean, maximal iff every g_ij≤0. For the specified g>0, the two contributions with a=g h_i/h_j and b=g h_j/h_i are at least (a+b+2g²)/(1+a+b+g²), strictly increasing in a+b since g<1. Equality requires equal heights and no extra positive pair. To check existence, take the two stated apices (±a,b,0) and a centered regular equatorial simplex of radius ρ. If m=d−1, the remaining gradients have y component −1/(bm); for m>1 their mutual products are 1/(bm)²−(m−1)/(m²ρ²), strictly negative for small ρ. Their products with the apical gradients are negative; for d=2 there is just one remaining gradient. This realizes each angle with the claimed equality. The four rational benchmark probabilities and the sum were independently recovered by cofactor inversion of the affine vertex matrix.
residual_risks: The benchmark replay is not a substitute for the all-dimensional proof. The result is about uniform variable center, not the single center of a uniformly dense simplex.

value.rationale: The exact active simplex quantifies the mass-center robustness of each natural support facet rather than testing a single center. The mean and a sharp shape-to-stability loss with equality characterize a measurable aspect of variable-center equilibrium distinct from all-strata counts. In particular, knowing an obtuse dihedral angle alone gives an optimal dimension-independent loss without reconstructing the shape.
residual_risks: Single-facet probabilities and their mean do not establish joint correlations or a general polytope formula.
